correctness.rationale: For linear indexed words the pair-count balance forces equality of endpoints by the divergence identity; on a closed path a divergence-free integer current vanishing on the cotree must vanish also on the tree. Orthogonality on the cotree torus gives the stated trace of H(θ)^{n−1}, including all q roots. The Hermitian eigenvalues are in [2−q,q], and equality at q in the triangle/Rayleigh bound requires all phases to be a vertex gauge; the star fixes this gauge, leaving exactly the zero point on the torus. Independently checking the Hessian, for a unit vector u the quadratic form of qI−H is ∑_{edges ij}|u_i−e^{iθ_ij}u_j|² with zero angles on the star. At zero the single minimizing vector is uniform up to phase; its analytic continuation has real and imaginary first variations. The leading energy minimizes a nonnegative real-gradient square and the imaginary-gradient square with imposed cochain Jθ/√q. The real gradient can vanish; projecting the imaginary residual onto the cycle space gives θ^T J^T P J θ/q. Both bounds follow by expanding the analytic minimizer and testing the minimizing first-order trial vector. Conjugation eliminates odd orders. The fundamental-cycle Gram matrix I+C^TC has determinant q^{q−2} by the complete-graph Laplacian on the nonroot vertices and Sylvester's identity. The spectral gap and positive Hessian justify Gaussian localization with determinant factor; dividing by q^{n}, not q^{n−1}, accounts for the additional 1/q. The binary H has constant eigenvalues 2,0 and gives the exact formula for n≥2 (n=1 is separately all letters). In the ternary cycle the three currents of a closed walk coincide, so the net signed increment is three times that common current; zero signed sum also implies closure. Counting balanced increments gives precisely the stated central trinomial sum including n=1. The supplied exhaustive and transfer programs plus verification notes were inspected, not run; the all-q result is supported by the analytic argument in RESULT.md lines 30–86.

originality.rationale: The general return-probability local central limit theorem for walks on crystal lattices covers the principal asymptotic under an equivalent exact model. This is not a priority judgment based on an inaccessible article or on nearby word-class counts. For q≥3 take the maximal free abelian cover of K_q with cotree coordinates from a star and give the simple walk holding probability 1/q. A uniform length-n word corresponds to L=n−1 of these steps with uniform start over base vertices. Its balanced-pair event is exactly return to the same lift: the base endpoint is the same and the integral cycle current is zero. Star triangles give all coordinate generators, verifying the full deck lattice Z^d. The covariance in these coordinates is elementary: correct the oriented edge increments J by a vertex coboundary to get the divergence-free representative PJ, which makes the corrected increments martingale differences. Stationary directed edges each have probability 1/q² (holding steps contribute zero), so Σ=2J^TPJ/q². The stationary mass of each base vertex is 1/q. The aperiodic crystal-walk return LLT gives (1/q)(2π L)^{−d/2}(det Σ)^{−1/2}; using the elementary fundamental-cycle Gram determinant q^{q−2} gives exactly the frozen constant. Alternatively remove the holding steps: the nonholding walk has period two (zero current forces an even number of traversals in total and a two-step reversal is possible). The period factor two cancels with the asymptotic even-parity probability one half under binomial mixing at time L(q−1)/q. Thus this implication does not depend on a loop convention for the prior theorem. The binary and ternary formulas are trivial endpoint and balanced-increment counts, with the latter not asserted new in the record. No separate nonmechanical remainder is supported.
